items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: when I hear Wynton with the Art Blakey band, he was playing the living hell out of the trumpet.

ctx.x: You know? So either you’re 17, you know or 20; or you’re 94 or something like this. And these are the people that are being recorded. And these — that is not the best era of a musician’s career, when you’re very, very young — I mean when I hear Wynton with the Art Blakey band, he was playing the living hell out of the trumpet. Whew. Man, that guy was playing some really great trumpet. So there are exceptions to this rule. But most of these contracts are going to these kids. And I think that’s why people aren’t…
those beautiful things, “I Loves You Porgy” and all of those kinds. And this is what’s happening. Marketing is like you know taking the art out of art.
